manifest.name: Audio Recognizer: AudD + Local Fingerprints
manifest.description: Recognizes music on live audio sources such as a turntable. Known tracks are recognized locally from fingerprints it learns; unknown tracks are identified by sending a short sample to AudD (a paid service with a free trial; API token required). A known track without a stored length is sent to AudD once, to learn it.

audd_api_token.label: AudD API token
audd_api_token.description: Needed to identify music the provider has not learned yet. Without a token only previously learned tracks are recognized (locally). AudD is a paid service with a free trial; get a token at https://dashboard.audd.io

all_audio_sources.label: Recognize all live audio sources
all_audio_sources.description: Advanced, off by default: normally you choose your sources (e.g. your turntable) under 'Audio sources to recognize'. Turn on only if every live audio source that allows analysis should be recognized.

audio_sources.label: Audio sources to recognize
audio_sources.description: Choose the live sources to recognize, e.g. your turntable. Nothing is recognized until you choose one.

silence_threshold_dbfs.label: Silence threshold (dBFS)
silence_threshold_dbfs.description: Audio at or below this level counts towards a track gap.

resume_threshold_dbfs.label: Resume threshold (dBFS)
resume_threshold_dbfs.description: Audio at or above this level ends a track gap.

minimum_gap_seconds.label: Minimum track gap (seconds)
minimum_gap_seconds.description: How long the silence must last to count as a track change.

save_audd_samples.label: Save AudD samples for debugging
save_audd_samples.description: Keep the last 250 audio samples sent to AudD, with their outcome and measurements, in the provider's data folder (debug/). Only for troubleshooting; they stay on this server.

record_input_stream.label: Record the input stream for debugging
record_input_stream.description: Temporarily record the live input exactly as the recognizer receives it (WAV, about 10 MB per minute), with the recognizer's log of each session, in the provider's data folder (recordings/), up to the maximum below; then it stops by itself. Only for troubleshooting recognition: every recording is deleted automatically 3 days after it started. The files stay on this server (and are included in Home Assistant backups meanwhile).

record_input_max_minutes.label: Maximum recording (minutes)
record_input_max_minutes.description: Total length of all input recordings kept on this server (about 10 MB per minute). When it is reached, recording stops until recordings are removed.

audd_speed_correction_percent.label: Speed correction for AudD (%)
audd_speed_correction_percent.description: If your turntable runs a little fast or slow, AudD may miss many tracks. Samples sent to AudD are played this much faster (positive) or slower (negative); e.g. -2 for a turntable that runs about 2 % fast. Local recognition is not affected. Measure your turntable with an RPM app.

fast_start.label: Faster recognition at the start of known tracks
fast_start.description: Stores more fingerprints of the first 30 seconds of every track, so a record you play again from the start is usually recognized within 12-18 seconds without asking AudD. Uses about 25 % more disk space; turn off for a very large collection. Applies to tracks learned (or played again) from now on.

audd_thorough.label: Ask AudD more often (live and gapless records)
audd_thorough.description: While music is still unidentified, ask AudD every 30 seconds instead of slowing down to every 90 seconds after three tries. Helps on live and gapless records, where tracks run into each other, but uses more AudD requests (about 8 instead of 5 for a 4-minute track AudD does not know).
